10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.

21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.

content.text:
Built a playable 3D shooting range in `index.html`. It includes six stationary targets, three switchable weapons, ballistic drop, recoil and spread, ammo and reloads, and keyboard, mouse, and touch controls.

Start the local server with `python3 -m http.server 3002` and open `http://localhost:3002`. Desktop controls: WASD to move, mouse to aim, click to fire, R to reload, 1–3 to switch weapons, and Esc to pause. I verified the page loads without console errors and saved the visual check to `screenshots/range.jpg`.

Assumption: “realistic physics” is represented by simplified ballistic bullet drop, recoil, and weapon-specific spread.
